titulo: One news item in several varieties
intro: Compare three fictional versions of the same local news item and notice regional vocabulary and forms of address.
p.colectivo: bus (used in Argentina and nearby varieties)
b1.texto: Many speakers in Spain use **vosotros** for an informal group; **ustedes** is usual across much of the Americas and also appears in parts of Spain. **Vos** is used in several American regions, with forms that vary. Bus vocabulary also varies: **autobús**, **camión** and **colectivo** are used in different places, but usage can differ by city and context. The examples below are fictional and show broad clues, not rules for every speaker or country.
b2.titulo: A local news item in three varieties
b2.f0: Madrid: The town council has opened a new bus route today. Have you all seen the notice? The stop is next to the market.
b2.f1: Mexico City: They opened a new bus route today. Have you all tried it yet? The stop is next to the market.
b2.f2: Buenos Aires: They opened a new bus route today. Have you tried it yet? The stop is next to the market.
b2.f3: The three texts report a similar development, but they do not use exactly the same words or forms of address. The context makes it clear that they are talking about a new transport route.
b2.f4: In the first version, «ha abierto» presents the development as connected to the present; the other two use simple past forms to report what happened today.
b2.f5: All three questions address the reader, but each shows a different form of address; «ustedes» does not always indicate formality.
b2.f6: Verb choice can vary by region and context, so one sentence is not enough to describe how an entire community speaks.
